paragraphs: BiblioCommons builds the online side of a public library, covering the catalog, mobile app, website, events calendar and email marketing. The pieces are sold as a suite intended to work as one.

BiblioCore is the discovery layer, presented as more than an online repository of a library's collections. Search uses facets and FRBRised grouping so patrons can find titles the way they search elsewhere on the web. Accessibility features include screen reader support, color contrast compliance, keyboard access, grouped search and text resizing. Reviews and lists contributed by patrons are shared across all BiblioCore libraries. Add-on modules offer interface languages ranging from Filipino, French, Japanese and Korean to Spanish and Vietnamese. Another synchronizes eContent metadata directly from providers so the collection shows in the catalog. BiblioFines integrates with PayPal and the ILS so patrons can settle payments online.

The catalog is vendor agnostic and integrates the products and services public libraries subscribe to. The company says it began as a non-profit youth literacy initiative before turning to library catalogs. Three Canadian provincial agencies funded prototypes and purchased advanced subscriptions in the early years. After a year-long beta with six libraries, the re-architected services were re-launched. Staff are described as coming from both technical and library backgrounds.
